biggest_gap.what: Rounds 9 and 10 put a contrapposto and then a root drop on the shared `idle_ready` stance layer, and BOTH REACH EXACTLY ONE DRAWN CHARACTER PLUS THE COMBAT ENEMIES. MEASURED IN THE RUNNING GAME, not read out of the source: at the Lilmoth crowd stand, reading `bone.matrixWorld` off the objects the renderer drew, all 60 drawn NPCs report hip-line dy = 0.000000 m and shoulder-line dy = 0.000000 m — exactly zero — while the player in the same frame reports -0.018289 m and +0.047948 m. `renderer.js:syncNPCs` calls `poseStatic` and only `poseStatic`; `poseStatic`'s own header reads 'Non-combat people use the rig's authored REST pose', and it binds presentation meshes once against `built.restWorld` and never evaluates a clip or a stance layer. So RI-VIS10 §F#6 — 'a symmetric A-pose with the arms lowered, identical on every NPC' — is present on every NPC in every settlement, unchanged by two rounds of work aimed squarely at it. THE r9 VERDICT'S OWN `why_it_matters` IS WRONG ON ITS NPC HALF: 'the player and all 408 NPCs, because the change is on the single shared idle_ready layer' — the LAYER is shared, the CODE PATH that applies it is not. The builder found this and re-derived it rather than inheriting it; I confirmed it in the running game, which is the arm it had not done. It also makes E4 worse than E4's own number says: the 93 adjacent duplicate pairs are not merely the same body, they are the same body in the same pose.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: A player walking into Lilmoth sees sixty people and one of them is posed. The stance work is the only part of F10 that has ever passed a design check, and it is invisible to the player everywhere except on their own character — who they mostly see from behind. This is the single largest gap between what the verdicts say F10 has achieved and what the owner would find if they opened the game right now.
biggest_gap.remedy: In `game/src/render/actor.js:poseStatic`, extend the existing ONE-TIME bind. It already caches under `A.staticPresentationBound` and already computes `built.restWorld`; add, inside that same block: (1) `addPose(rig, clips.archetypes.idle_ready, 0, 1.0)` plus `stanceRootOffsetY(idle_ready, 0, 1.0)` baked into the rest matrices before the presentation meshes are bound, so every NPC gets the contrapposto AND the root drop that keeps its feet on the floor; and (2) a per-NPC phase offset `FNV1a('npc:'+eid) % idle_loop.period` sampled into the same bake, so the crowd is not frozen at one point of one breathing cycle. Per-frame cost is unchanged — this is a one-time bind, not a per-frame evaluation. DONE means: `node tools/visual/f10-r10c-npc-live.mjs --x 2785.6 --z 5047.0` reports (a) `npc_hip_line_dy_m.max_abs` >= 0.010 and `npc_shoulder_line_dy_m.max_abs` >= 0.030 — i.e. the crowd carries the same stance the player does — and (b) `npc_pose_signatures.distinct` >= 8 over >= 50 drawn NPCs, which is the phase-offset arm and cannot be satisfied by the stance alone. PRESERVATION per S59, and it is the clause that stops (a) being bought by shoving the crowd through the floor: every drawn NPC's `foot_l_y` and `foot_r_y` must stay within 2 mm of its own pre-change value at the same stand, and `node tools/harness/anim-tune.mjs` must still report 0 of 14 over 0.35 m with worst snapOut <= 0.0122 m.

arbitration_questions.question: The r9 verdict's `DONE means` includes `after.lr_diff_max_m` no worse than the before arm's 0.00109 m. Round 10 reports 0.00521, ruled against chasing it, and named its own overturn condition: 'overturned if the 5.2 mm reads as visible in frames.' Is the clause met, and if not, is it the build or the criterion that is wrong?
arbitration_questions.my_ruling: THE BUILDER'S RULING STANDS. THE CLAUSE IS VOID AS WRITTEN AND THE FAULT IS THE CRITERION'S, NOT THE BUILD'S — this is S59's own shape, arriving from the other side. I answered the overturn condition on hardware, which is the one thing only a critic could do. THE 5.2 mm IS NOT VISIBLE. (1) Arithmetic, published: the CP capture stands at 2.486 m and renders 376.2 px/m at 1080 rows, so 5.2 mm is 1.96 px. The camera a player actually orbits at is `CAMERA_CONST.arm_free_m` = 4.10 m (`game/src/sim/camera.js:63`), where it is 1.19 px at 1080p and 0.59 px at the harness's own 960x540 default — so my capture is a MORE generous test than gameplay, not a less generous one. (2) Look, published: at 6x with a ruled grid, the two soles in the AFTER arm are already 13 px apart for a reason that has nothing to do with height — one foot stands 17 mm nearer the camera and the perspective term dominates the height term by 6:1. (3) Noise floor, measured: the boot band's mean luma-sum is 74.7 of 765 under a dither whose per-pixel standard deviation is 45.4. A sub-2-px edge shift inside a near-black dithered region is not a thing an eye recovers. (4) The structural argument is also correct and I checked it: 0.00109 was the difference of two IDENTICAL legs under an ANTI-symmetric loop, and contrapposto requires the legs to be geometrically different (155.4 deg against 171.9 deg), so the same +-0.52 deg loop rotation produces a different vertical response on each. The builder's search reproduces exactly on its own instrument — 1-DOF floor 0.00260, 2-DOF 0.00260, 3-DOF 0.00228 and only by inverting the breathing loop's own amplitude. AND ROUND 10 DID NOT CAUSE IT: on hardware the drawn per-foot difference is 0.0052 m in BOTH arms, so this is r9's number inherited, not r10's regression. REPLACEMENT CLAUSE, both parts required: (a) `after.lr_diff_max_m` <= 0.00600 m — the value the contrapposto structurally implies, with headroom, and a real bound because 0.00521 sits under it; and (b) PRESERVATION, which is what the original clause was reaching for and named the wrong quantity for: the LOWER ankle's absolute height above ground must stay within 1 mm of the pre-contrapposto baseline, measured on the built rig across the full 96-frame loop. On this build (b) reads 0.07770 m against a baseline 0.07774 m — 0.04 mm — so the substance the clause wanted is met.
arbitration_questions.what_would_overturn_it: A capture at the game's real presentation resolution and lighting in which a reader who was not told what to look for identifies one foot as sitting higher than the other. My frames are 1920x1080 on an RTX A5000 with the sun where the game puts it, and it does not happen.

arbitration_questions.question: The r9 verdict's `DONE means` also names `node tools/visual/f10-r9c-c3-audit.mjs` reporting `B_feet.summary.rise_of_lower_ankle_m.mean` within 1 mm of 0. Run unmodified on this tree it still reports 0.00796. Does F10 r10's job 1 fail?
arbitration_questions.my_ruling: NO. THE CRITERION IS VOID AS WRITTEN — S60 ALMOST VERBATIM, AND THE FAULT IS THE r9 CRITIC'S, WHICH IS TO SAY IT IS THE INSTRUMENT I INHERITED. `f10-r9c-c3-audit.mjs`'s `pose()` reproduces `poseLocomotion` as it stood BEFORE round 10 and computes `rootDy` from the LOOP only, so it structurally cannot see a stance-layer root term. **The metric is evaluated off the support of the thing it measures**: no fix of this shape can ever turn it green, and a build that deleted the stance entirely would score better on it than a build that compensated the stance correctly. The builder refused to edit it — 'editing a critic's acceptance instrument to agree with my own fix is metric-shopping' — and that was the right call and is why the disagreement is visible at all. I SETTLED IT WITH AN INSTRUMENT THAT HAS NO STAKE IN EITHER ARM: the paid RTX A5000 frames. At the flat player stand, ground = 2.680 m in BOTH arms and identical to 4 decimals, the drawn foot bones go foot_l 2.7761 -> 2.7681 (-8.0 mm) and foot_r 2.7812 -> 2.7733 (-7.9 mm). Against the pre-contrapposto baseline the r9 critic itself photographed (0.0890 / 0.0901 above ground), round 10's lower ankle sits at 0.0881 — 0.9 mm BELOW the original baseline, i.e. the hover is gone. My BEFORE arm reproduces the r9 critic's AFTER arm to the digit (0.0961 / 0.1012), which cross-checks two independently written capture tools against each other. THE SUBSTANCE OF THE CLAUSE IS MET. REPLACEMENT: name `tools/visual/f10-r10-stance-height.mjs`'s `A_states.IDLE.rise_vs_before_engine_r10_m` (0.00000 on this build) or the hardware manifest's `slope_stands[char-player].measured.foot_l.y` minus `.ground`, not the r9 tool. The r9 tool needs a one-line mirror of `actor.js:401` before it is quoted again by anybody.

secondary_observations.note: PAID HARDWARE, ONE POD, ONE PROCESS, FOUR FILES SWAPPED TOGETHER. `f10-r9c-stance-pair.mjs` could not shoot this pair: it swaps ONE file against a baseline pinned to r9's own before, and round 10's change is spread over four files with `15a6841c` as its base. Swapping only `clips.json` would have put r10's DATA under r9's CODE — a `root_offset` nothing consumes — and produced a sheet that looked like evidence and contained none. So `f10-r10c-pair.mjs` moves all four together, each pinned by sha256 at the swap and again at the restore, with self-test arms that require `stanceRootOffsetY` to be defined AND called in exactly one arm. The builder also published the number that moved the WRONG way and I confirm it: the WALK/RUN/SPRINT loop MEAN is still +7.3 / +9.2 / +10.7 mm high, because the mean averages the planted foot with a swinging one that the shortened free leg lifts higher. CHECKED, BECAUSE THE BRIEF WAS RIGHT TO FLAG IT. Before r10, `block_hold.root_offset.y = -0.03` was dead data — `addPose` iterated `tracks` only. Round 10 taught the engine to read `root_offset`, which would have made that 3 cm LIVE. `root_offset` translates the WHOLE rig, feet included, so it is not a crouch: it would have put every guarding character's soles 30 mm under the ground. The builder zeroed it. VERIFIED THREE WAYS: (1) the code path — `actor.js:401` passes `this.moves._blockPose` to `stanceRootOffsetY`, which returns 0 for `[[0,0],[3,0]]`; (2) the measurement — IDLE_GUARD, WALK_GUARD, RUN_GUARD and SPRINT_GUARD all read IDENTICAL rise values on the pre-r10 and post-r10 engines (-0.00097 and 0.00000), so guarding behaviour is unchanged in both directions; (3) the record — `clips.json`'s own `block_hold.note` now carries the deletion, its reason and the condition for restoring it ('a real guard crouch needs knee tracks first'). An authored intention was deleted; it was deleted in the data, in writing, with its restoration condition. That is the right way to do it and I would have failed it if it had been done silently.

Eight bearings on an RTX A5000, whole figure in frame. A pale blue-grey padded barrel with no waist, on two thick parallel tubes that end in olive drums. A small dark head with a muzzle and two cone spikes. A very long dark tail sweeping out behind — real geometry, and it reads more like a scorpion's sting than a lizard's tail: it is as long as a leg, curves up and then to a point, and is rooted high. A black hexagonal shield slab and a greatsword crossing the body. At every one of the eight bearings both legs are vertical and parallel, the boots are level and shoulder-width, and the pelvis is not displaced over either leg. THE CONTRAPPOSTO THAT PASSES C3 AT 5 DEGREES IS NOT LEGIBLE AS A STANCE AT THE DISTANCE A PLAYER STANDS. The r9 critic wrote that C3's 3 degrees is 'a floor, not a target' and I am confirming it from a different capture: the difference between the arms is visible in a difference mask and is not visible as a person shifting their weight.

ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS 'NOTHING EARLIER'. `tools/harness/anim-tune.mjs` reproduces `poseLocomotion` rather than calling it, and until this round it omitted the stance root term. BUT the stance root term did not exist until this round: my pair runner's self-test arm 4 confirms that at `15a6841c` neither `clips.js` nor `combat/actor.js` contains the string `stanceRootOffsetY`, and `addPose` read `tracks` only. So the harness was not blind before r10 — it became blind at the instant r10's job 1 landed, and r10 corrected it in the same commit. NO EARLIER GREEN READING RESTS ON THE OMISSION. What DOES rest on it, and is the finding worth keeping, is structural: the harness holds a SECOND COPY of `poseLocomotion`, so every future change to the real one silently desynchronises the gate that protects the attack/idle boundary. That is `HAZARDS §20a`'s shape (a generator holding a second copy of the idle) arriving in a different file. Round 10 papered it with a comment; it should be a call into `poseLocomotion`, or a test that asserts the two agree.

OVERTURNED, ON A COPY, AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS BECAUSE IT CHANGES THE FIX. The round records `swing.js`'s `r2()` as 'two decimal places… the smallest value it can emit is 10 mm' and concludes 'fixing the generator needs a precision change, not a value change'. `game/src/combat/swing.js:64` is `Math.round(x * 1000) / 1000` — THREE decimals; the smallest step is 1 mm and -0.00796 would survive rounding as -0.008, an error of 0.04 mm. The endpoints die at lines 311-318, where `rootY` is built from HARD-CODED LITERALS — `[0.0, 0.0]` at phase 0, `[3.0, -0.01 + cr*0.25]` at phase 3 — with no stance term in the expression at all. REPRODUCED: `git archive HEAD` to a scratch tree, `node tools/harness/anim-author.mjs --only thrust --out <scratch>`, and `thrust.root_offset.y` comes back `[[0,0],…,[3,0]]` against a shipped `[[0,-0.00796],…,[3,-0.00796]]`. So the round's WARNING is right and urgent and its DIAGNOSIS would have sent the next builder to widen a rounding function that is already wide enough. Filed as HAZARDS §20d. The same run re-derives §20a: `idle_loop` `spine_00.rx` 0.68 -> 0.45 and `neck.rx` 0.75 -> 0.5, 33.8% and 33.3% shrinks of the hand-tuned breathing, still live.

RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS THE FAILURE SHAPE HAZARDS §0 NAMES. My first NPC probe hashed each bone's LOCAL quaternion into a pose signature, and reported the player and all 60 NPCs sharing ONE identical signature — which would have 'confirmed' the finding I was sent to test, spectacularly and wrongly. `poseFromRig` writes bone WORLD matrices and never touches the local quaternion, so a local-rotation reader is blind to the player's pose by construction. Self-test arm 1 — 'the player's signature must DIFFER from the modal NPC signature' — went red and caught it. The corrected reader takes `inverse(group.matrixWorld) * bone.matrixWorld`, which is path-agnostic. The finding survived the correction; the point is that a self-test arm whose job is to fail when the instrument agrees too easily is what stood between this verdict and a confidently wrong headline.
